pairs.subject: serving-process-topology
pairs.evidence: crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:175 Each agent run spawns one fresh CLI child from its own run directory, with no replicas, no latency-budget hot loop and no choice of how to create it; searching crates/table-engine for replica, latency, fork, start_method and load balanc found nothing, so the subject's precondition (a latency-critical serving service split into processes) does not hold.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-engine/src/windows_job.rs:51 No loop whose period is a product latency figure (per-run stream reader with init/total watchdogs), so isolation does not apply; the Step-6 reaper sub-rule is still realized: suspended child assigned to a kill-on-close job before its first instruction, plus kill_on_drop and lock-guarded stale-run reaping.
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:174 Rust Command always fresh-starts the child (CreateProcess); there is no copy-the-parent vs start-fresh choice and no strategy knob to probe for or against.
crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:18 Shallow hierarchy (NativeEngine takes id, executable, root and a two-field RunLimits); the technique's 'when not to use: a shallow hierarchy' holds.

crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:167 Each run is a fresh child with session persistence disabled and its own run directory; no state is reused between requests and there is no replica set to balance.

crates/table-engine/src/native.rs:102 This crate only creates one child per run id; the concurrent-run cap lives in the runtime (MAX_RUNS) and there is no operator-provisioned deployment with independent knobs.

pairs.subject: serving-process-topology
pairs.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:537 The runtime is one in-process actor task on a 1-second publish tick that serializes wallet commands; it has no replicas, no inference loop with a latency budget and no process-creation strategy, and searching crates/table-runtime/src for replica, latency, fork, start_method and load balanc found nothing, so the subject's precondition does not hold.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:587 The actor loop's period is a 1 s housekeeping tick, not a product latency unit ('no sentence' case); it awaits runtime.execute inline (line 601), which would be a blocking hand-off only if a latency budget existed.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:16 Desktop app with no operator provisioning; the only child-process count is a single stated cap of 4 live agent runs (refused at engines.rs:203), not a product of independent deployment knobs.

crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:117 Engines are found by probing the environment (PATH and npm layout, then --version) rather than by configuration, which is in the technique's spirit, but no process-creation strategy is chosen here.
crates/table-runtime/src/engines.rs:131 Two-layer construction with defaulted limits; there is no deep configuration hierarchy to thread options through.
crates/table-runtime/src/actor.rs:526 A single actor drains one bounded queue; no replicas and no balancer, so replica affinity never comes up.
